clue.text: 16A old man's holding up map the wrong way round

definitions.note: 16A is PLAIN; pampas is a plural noun for the plains of South America

indicators.note: something the wrong way round faces backwards, so the word is read from its end
in a down entry, holding up means supporting from below, so this piece sits under the other

blocks.note: taken as written
pa is an informal word for father, plus the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: An old man holds a map upside down while lost on open grassland.
explanation.walkthrough: 16A refers to PLAIN. 'Holding' tempts you to put one piece inside the other, but in this down light PA'S sits below the reversed map, supporting it.
explanation.definitionFit: The pampas are the vast treeless grasslands of Argentina, a classic example of a plain.

clue.text: A famous 17, 17, 17 film with Sandra Bullock

explanation.surface: A trivia question about a well-known movie starring Sandra Bullock.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 is the answer BOB, used first as a name (Bob Hope) and then as a verb meaning to float on water.
explanation.definitionFit: Hope Floats is a 1998 romantic drama in which Sandra Bullock played the lead role.

clue.text: Secretary left without the FT is livid

clue.text: What you 17 for is relevant, bar one

explanation.surface: A comment that what you are searching for is pertinent, with one exception.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 is BOB: bobbing for apples is a party game of catching floating apples with your teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: In the game of bobbing, players try to grab fruit floating in a tub of water using only their mouths.

clue.text: New dustmen are not sorted by academic ability

explanation.surface: Newly hired refuse collectors have not been grouped by how clever they are.
explanation.walkthrough: Streaming is the British school practice of putting pupils into classes by ability.
explanation.definitionFit: An unstreamed class mixes pupils of all abilities instead of dividing them into ranked groups.

clue.text: Swap last pair then middle pair of 3, ringing changes

indicators.text: Swap last pair then middle pair
indicators.note: exchanging two adjacent letters, twice over, gives a precise rearrangement of the word

blocks.note: the answer to 3 down

explanation.walkthrough: PALE becomes PAEL when its last two letters swap, then PEAL when its middle two swap, mimicking how ringers swap adjacent bells.
explanation.definitionFit: A peal is a long series of changes rung on a set of church bells.

clue.text: Person using ticket in response to offer

explanation.definitionFit: An attender is someone present at an event, typically admitted by showing a ticket.

clue.text: Nose traveller follows back from India

the Roma are a traditionally travelling people

explanation.definitionFit: Nose is a wine-tasting term for the smell or bouquet of a drink.

clue.text: Relative starts to do elegant swan impression

explanation.walkthrough: Relative looks like a noun for a family member, but here it is the adjective, as in relative to.

an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.definitionFit: The deep web is the part of the internet that search engines do not index, so it stays hidden.

clue.text: Pastry Lee Mack shortly demolished, bit by bit

taken as written

clue.text: Flat ceramic includes date mark in Spanish

clue.text: Jointly take bananas to lost property?

explanation.walkthrough: A bunch of bananas is called a hand, and to take a found item to lost property is to hand it in.
explanation.definitionFit: Hand in hand means closely together, as partners act jointly in a shared venture.

clue.text: Staggered by 16A and D

taken as written

clue.text: Miniature portrait of Victoria, 12 for a 17?

explanation.walkthrough: A bob was the British shilling, worth twelve pre-decimal pennies; the 12 here is a number, not a clue reference.

clue.text: Builder who's 27 29 when the job's done

clue.text: Curving flight of e.g. fly cut in half - what keeps it up?

explanation.walkthrough: Inswing is a cricket term: a bowled ball that curves in the air towards the batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, a delivery's swing is its sideways curve through the air, and inward swing moves toward the batter.

clue.text: Quickly deflate favourite doll
